title: Electrical Equipment Use Checklist (29 CFR 1910.334)
subtitle: For supervisors checking an area where extension cords, corded tools, circuits or test instruments are in use.
instructions: Mark every item OK, Defect or N/A.
If an item fails, stop use of the equipment or task concerned, remove any damaged item from service and record the corrective action before work continues.
The manufacturer's instructions and your site rules may add checks to this list.

sections.title: Cords and portable equipment
items: No equipment is being raised or lowered by its flexible cord.
No cords held with staples or hung in a way that could damage the jacket or insulation.
No loose parts, deformed or missing pins, or jacket or insulation damage on cords and equipment.
No pinched or crushed sections of outer jacket.
Items were visually inspected before use on this shift, or have stayed connected in place, unexposed to damage and not relocated.
Any item with damage that could injure an employee is withdrawn and not used until repaired and tested.
Plug and receptacle contacts are proper mating configurations before connection.

sections.title: Grounding and plug connections
items: Cords used with grounding-type equipment contain an equipment grounding conductor.
No plug or receptacle connected or altered so the ground path is broken where they meet.
No plug or receptacle altered to let the grounding pole enter a current-carrying slot.
No adapter in use that interrupts the grounding connection.
Equipment and cords used where water or conductive liquids are present or likely to be contacted are approved for that location.
Workers plugging or unplugging energized equipment have dry hands.
Insulating protective equipment is used to handle any energized connection that could conduct to the hand, such as a wet connector.
Locking-type connectors are fully secured after connection.

sections.title: Circuits and overcurrent protection
items: Circuits under load are opened, reversed or closed only with load rated switches, breakers or designed disconnecting means.
Non-load-break connectors, fuses, terminal lugs and splices are not used to switch loaded circuits outside an emergency.
Tripped circuits are not manually reenergized until someone has determined the circuit and equipment can be safely energized.
No repeated manual resetting of breakers or reenergizing through replaced fuses.
Overcurrent protection is not modified, even temporarily, beyond what 1910.304(e) allows.

sections.title: Test instruments and flammable materials
items: Testing work on electric circuits or equipment is done only by qualified persons.
Test instruments, leads, cables, power cords, probes and connectors were visually inspected before use and show no external damage.
Damaged test gear that could injure an employee is withdrawn until repaired and tested.
Instruments and accessories are rated for the circuits and equipment they connect to.
Instruments and accessories are designed for the environment where they are used.
Where flammable gases, vapors, liquids, combustible dust or ignitible fibers are occasionally present, equipment able to ignite them is not used unless measures prevent hazardous conditions.

references: 29 CFR 1910.334: Use of equipment (Part 1910 Subpart S: Electrical)
